questions.explanation_english:
Form 16 consists of two distinct parts:

1. Part A: It is a standardized, digitally signed document downloaded directly by the employer from the TRACES (TDS Reconciliation Analysis and Correction Enabling System) portal of the Income Tax Department. It contains:
   - Name, address, PAN, and TAN of the employer/deductor.
   - Name, address, and PAN of the employee.
   - Summary of quarterly tax deducted (from Form 24Q filings) and actual date and challan identification details (BSR code, challan serial number) of tax deposited into the Central Government account.

2. Part B: Prepared by the employer (annexed to Part A), detailing gross salary, exempt allowances under Section 10 (e.g. HRA, conveyance), standard deduction under Section 16(ia), deductions under Chapter VI-A (80C, 80D, etc.), net taxable income, and final tax computation.

questions.question_english:
Consider the following steps for computing Income Tax on Salary:
I. Compute Gross Salary.
II. Deduct Standard Deduction, Professional Tax, and Entertainment Allowance (if applicable) to get Net Salary.
III. Add Income from other heads and apply Chapter VI-A deductions to find Total Taxable Income.
IV. Apply tax slab rates and add Surcharge / Health and Education Cess.
What is the correct sequential order of the above steps?
options_english: I, III, II, IV
I, II, III, IV
II, I, III, IV
I, IV, II, III
questions.explanation_english: The computation of taxable income and tax liability on salary follows a strict statutory hierarchy under the Income Tax Act, 1961: (1) Compute Gross Salary under Section 17; (2) Deduct statutory deductions under Section 16 (Standard Deduction up to ₹50,000, Entertainment Allowance under Section 16(ii), and Professional Tax under Section 16(iii)) to arrive at 'Income under the Head Salaries'; (3) Aggregate with permissible income/losses from other heads (such as House Property or Other Sources) and subtract eligible deductions under Chapter VI-A (Sections 80C to 80U) to arrive at Total Taxable Income; (4) Apply the applicable slab rates under the chosen tax regime, deduct rebates under Section 87A, and finally add 4% Health and Education Cess plus any applicable surcharge.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर B (I, II, III, IV) है। आयकर अधिनियम, 1961 के तहत वेतन पर आयकर की गणना एक निर्धारित वैधानिक क्रम में होती है: सर्वप्रथम धारा 17 के तहत सकल वेतन की गणना की जाती है; दूसरे चरण में धारा 16 के तहत अनुमन्य कटौतियाँ (₹50,000 की मानक कटौती, व्यावसायिक कर आदि) घटाकर वेतन शीर्ष से शुद्ध आय ज्ञात की जाती है; तीसरे चरण में अन्य शीर्षों की आय जोड़कर तथा अध्याय VI-A (धारा 80C से 80U) की कटौतियाँ घटाकर कुल कर योग्य आय निकाली जाती है; और चौथे चरण में लागू कर स्लैब दरें लगाकर 4% स्वास्थ्य एवं शिक्षा उपकर तथा अधिभार जोड़कर अंतिम कर देयता निर्धारित की जाती है।

questions.question_english:
Consider the following statements regarding the Standard Deduction available under Section 16(ia) for salaried taxpayers:
I. It is available uniformly as a flat deduction regardless of the actual expenses incurred by the employee.
II. It was reintroduced in lieu of the earlier tax exemptions for transport allowance and medical reimbursement.
III. Pensioners drawing pension taxable under the head 'Salaries' are also entitled to this deduction.
IV. The allowable deduction amount is prorated based on the number of months the employee worked in that financial year.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.question_hindi:
वेतनभोगी करदाताओं के लिए धारा 16(ia) के तहत उपलब्ध मानक कटौती (Standard Deduction) के संबंध में निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:
I. यह कर्मचारी द्वारा किए गए वास्तविक खर्चों की परवाह किए बिना एकमुश्त कटौती के रूप में समान रूप से उपलब्ध है।
II. इसे परिवहन भत्ता और चिकित्सा प्रतिपूर्ति पर मिलने वाली पूर्ववर्ती कर छूटों के स्थान पर पुनः लागू किया गया था।
III. 'वेतन' शीर्षक के तहत कर-योग्य पेंशन प्राप्त करने वाले पेंशनभोगी भी इस कटौती के पात्र हैं।
IV. अनुमत कटौती की राशि कर्मचारी द्वारा उस वित्तीय वर्ष में काम किए गए महीनों की संख्या के अनुपात में निर्धारित की जाती है।
उपर्युक्त कथनों में से कौन-से सही हैं?
options_english: I, II, and III only
II, III, and IV only
I and III only
I, II, III, and IV
options_hindi: केवल I, II और III
केवल II, III और IV
केवल I और III
I, II, III और IV
questions.explanation_english:
Statement I is correct: Standard deduction under Section 16(ia) is a statutory flat deduction available to all salaried taxpayers without requiring proof of any actual expenditure.
Statement II is correct: Finance Act 2018 reintroduced standard deduction to simplify tax compliance, replacing the earlier annual exemptions of ₹19,200 for transport allowance and ₹15,000 for medical reimbursement.
Statement III is correct: Pension received from a former employer is treated as salary under Section 17(1)(ii) of the Income Tax Act; hence, pensioners drawing such taxable pension are fully entitled to claim standard deduction up to ₹50,000.
Statement IV is incorrect: The standard deduction is an absolute statutory ceiling (₹50,000 or salary income, whichever is less) and is NOT prorated or calculated proportionally according to the number of months worked during the financial year. Even if an employee works for only a few months or days in the financial year, the full deduction up to their salary amount (subject to ₹50,000) is allowed.
Therefore, Statements I, II, and III only are correct.
questions.explanation_hindi:
कथन I सही है: धारा 16(ia) के तहत मानक कटौती एक वैधानिक एकमुश्त कटौती है जो कर्मचारी द्वारा किए गए किसी भी वास्तविक खर्च के प्रमाण के बिना सभी वेतनभोगियों को मिलती है।
कथन II सही है: वित्त अधिनियम 2018 द्वारा अनुपालन को सरल बनाने के लिए पूर्व में मिलने वाली ₹19,200 की परिवहन भत्ता छूट तथा ₹15,000 की चिकित्सा प्रतिपूर्ति छूट को समाप्त करके उसके स्थान पर मानक कटौती को पुनः लाया गया था।
कथन III सही है: पूर्व नियोक्ता से प्राप्त पेंशन को धारा 17(1)(ii) के तहत वेतन माना जाता है, इसलिए 'वेतन' शीर्षक में पेंशन दर्शाने वाले पेंशनभोगी भी ₹50,000 तक की मानक कटौती के पूर्ण पात्र हैं।
कथन IV गलत है: मानक कटौती की राशि वित्तीय वर्ष में काम किए गए महीनों के अनुपात (pro-rata) में निर्धारित नहीं होती। यदि किसी कर्मचारी ने वर्ष में कुछ महीने या दिन भी कार्य किया है, तब भी उसे उसके वेतन की सीमा तक पूरी ₹50,000 की कटौती की पात्रता होती है।
अतः केवल कथन I, II और III सही हैं।

questions.question_english:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): The issuance of Form 16 by the employer is a statutory obligation, and failure to issue it attracts a penalty under Section 272A(2)(g) of the Income Tax Act.
Reason (R): Form 16 is essential for salaried employees to verify tax deductions at source and file their income tax returns accurately.
In the context of the statements above, which of the following is correct?
questions.question_hindi:
नीचे दो कथन दिए गए हैं: एक को अभिकथन (A) और दूसरे को कारण (R) कहा गया है:
अभिकथन (A): नियोक्ता द्वारा फॉर्म 16 जारी करना एक वैधानिक दायित्व है और इसे निर्धारित समय में जारी न करने पर आयकर अधिनियम की धारा 272A(2)(g) के तहत शास्ति (जुर्माना) देय होती है।
कारण (R): फॉर्म 16 वेतनभोगी कर्मचारियों के लिए स्रोत पर कर कटौती (TDS) को सत्यापित करने और अपने आयकर रिटर्न को सही ढंग से दाखिल करने के लिए अनिवार्य दस्तावेज है।
उपर्युक्त कथनों के संदर्भ में, निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा सही है?
options_english: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is true, but (R) is false.
(A) is false, but (R) is true.
options_hindi: (A) और (R) दोनों सही हैं और (R), (A) की सही व्याख्या है।
(A) और (R) दोनों सही हैं, लेकिन (R), (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं है।
(A) सही है, लेकिन (R) गलत है।
(A) गलत है, लेकिन (R) सही है।
questions.explanation_english: Under Section 203 of the Income Tax Act, 1961 read with Rule 31 of the Income Tax Rules, every Drawing and Disbursing Officer (DDO) or employer deducting tax at source under Section 192 is statutorily mandated to furnish a certificate of tax deduction in Form 16 to the employee by 15th June of the relevant Assessment Year. Failure to issue Form 16 within the prescribed statutory due date attracts a penalty under Section 272A(2)(g) of the Act (₹500 for every day during which the failure continues). Reason (R) correctly explains why this statutory compulsion exists: Form 16 consists of Part A (TRACES-generated TDS deposit details) and Part B (salary breakdown, exemptions, and Chapter VI-A deductions), which serve as conclusive proof of TDS and enable salaried employees to verify tax credits against Form 26AS/AIS and accurately prepare and file their annual Income Tax Return under Section 139(1). Thus, both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation_hindi: आयकर अधिनियम, 1961 की धारा 203 और आयकर नियमावली के नियम 31 के तहत, धारा 192 के अधीन वेतन से स्रोत पर कर कटौती (TDS) करने वाले प्रत्येक आहरण एवं संवितरण अधिकारी (DDO)/नियोक्ता का यह वैधानिक दायित्व है कि वह संबंधित कर निर्धारण वर्ष की 15 जून तक कर्मचारी को फॉर्म 16 जारी करे। निर्धारित तिथि तक फॉर्म 16 जारी करने में विफल रहने पर धारा 272A(2)(g) के तहत प्रतिदिन ₹500 का जुर्माना लगाया जाता है। कारण (R) इसकी बिल्कुल सही व्याख्या करता है: फॉर्म 16 (भाग क एवं भाग ख) में कर्मचारी के वेतन, कटौतियों एवं सरकारी खाते में जमा किए गए TDS का प्रामाणिक विवरण होता है, जिसके बिना कर्मचारी 26AS/AIS से मिलान करके धारा 139(1) के तहत अपना आयकर रिटर्न सही-सही दाखिल नहीं कर सकता। अतः (A) और (R) दोनों सही हैं और (R), (A) की सही व्याख्या है।

questions.question_english: If a government school teacher is posted in a remote hilly area and receives a Special Compensatory (Hill Areas) Allowance, under which section of the Income Tax Act, 1961, is it eligible for partial tax exemption?
options_english: Section 10(10)
Section 10(14)

Section 16(ii)
questions.explanation_english:
Under Section 10(14)(ii) of the Income Tax Act, 1961 read with Rule 2BB(2) (Item 1 in the Table) of the Income-tax Rules, 1962:
1. Special compensatory allowances granted to employees posted in designated high-altitude, difficult, or remote hilly areas (such as the Special Compensatory Hill Areas Allowance) are eligible for partial tax exemption.
2. The statutory exemption limit ranges from ₹300 to ₹7,000 per month depending on the altitude and designated composite area/category.
Other provisions:
- Section 10(10) governs exemptions on gratuity.
- Section 10(5) governs Leave Travel Concession (LTC).
- Section 16(ii) provides statutory deductions for entertainment allowance for government employees.
Thus, Section 10(14) is the correct section.
questions.explanation_hindi:
आयकर अधिनियम, 1961 की धारा 10(14)(ii) तथा आयकर नियम के नियम 2BB(2) के अंतर्गत:
1. विशिष्ट दूरस्थ, उच्च-पर्वतीय या कठिन परिस्थितियों वाले क्षेत्रों में सेवा करने के कारण दिए जाने वाले विशेष प्रतिपूरक भत्ते (जैसे Hill Areas Allowance / High Altitude Allowance) आंशिक आयकर छूट के लिए पात्र हैं।
2. यह छूट ऊंचाई और निर्दिष्ट भौगोलिक क्षेत्र के आधार पर ₹300 प्रति माह से लेकर ₹7,000 प्रति माह तक निर्धारित सीमाओं के अधीन होती है।
अन्य विकल्पों में:

Under Rule 2B(2) of the Income Tax Rules, 1962, if an employee has not availed the Leave Travel Concession (LTC/LTA) exemption in respect of one or both of the two journeys permitted during a four-calendar-year block, they are entitled to carry over ONE unutilized journey to the immediately succeeding four-year block.
However, to claim tax exemption for this carried-over journey, the employee MUST perform that journey in the FIRST calendar year of the immediately succeeding block. If availed in that first calendar year, it does not count against the regular quota of two journeys permitted for that new block, effectively allowing three exempt journeys in that block.

questions.question_english: Which of the following correctly defines a "Composite Supply" under Section 2(30) of the CGST Act, 2017, which is particularly relevant when schools bundle educational and ancillary services?
options_english: A supply of two or more independent goods or services bundled together where all items are taxed at the highest applicable slab rate

A supply involving exclusively non-taxable export goods and offshore digital educational content

questions.explanation_english: Under Section 2(30) of the CGST Act, 2017, a 'Composite Supply' means a supply made by a taxable person to a recipient consisting of two or more taxable supplies of goods or services or both, or any combination thereof, which are naturally bundled and supplied in conjunction with each other in the ordinary course of business, one of which is a principal supply. Under Section 8(a), the tax liability on a composite supply is determined entirely by the tax rate applicable to the principal supply. For instance, in a residential school providing education along with lodging and boarding, the principal supply is education; since schooling up to higher secondary level is exempt from GST under Entry 66 of Notification No. 12/2017-Central Tax (Rate), the entire composite package enjoys exemption. In contrast, artificially bundled supplies sold for a single price are 'Mixed Supplies' under Section 2(74) and taxed at the highest rate under Section 8(b).
questions.explanation_hindi: CGST अधिनियम, 2017 की धारा 2(30) के अनुसार, 'संयुक्त आपूर्ति' (Composite Supply) से तात्पर्य किसी करदाता द्वारा प्राप्तकर्ता को की गई वस्तुओं या सेवाओं की दो या दो से अधिक ऐसी आपूर्तियों से है जो सामान्य व्यावसायिक व्यवहार में स्वाभाविक रूप से एक साथ जुड़ी (naturally bundled) होती हैं, जिनमें से एक 'मुख्य आपूर्ति' (Principal Supply) होती है। धारा 8(a) के प्रावधानों के अनुसार, ऐसी संपूर्ण संयुक्त आपूर्ति पर मुख्य आपूर्ति की दर से ही कर लगाया जाता है। उदाहरण के लिए, किसी आवासीय (बोर्डिंग) स्कूल द्वारा विद्यार्थियों को शिक्षा के साथ-साथ छात्रावास और भोजन प्रदान करना एक स्वाभाविक रूप से बंडल संयुक्त आपूर्ति है, जिसमें मुख्य आपूर्ति 'शिक्षा' है। चूंकि विद्यालयी शिक्षा अधिसूचना सं. 12/2017 के तहत कर-मुक्त है, इसलिए पूरे पैकेज को छूट मिलती है। इसके विपरीत, अस्वाभाविक रूप से बंडल की गई आपूर्ति धारा 2(74) के तहत 'मिश्रित आपूर्ति' (Mixed Supply) कहलाती है और धारा 8(b) के तहत उन पर उच्चतम दर से कर लगता है।

Under Section 2(30) of the CGST Act, a Composite Supply comprises two or more naturally bundled taxable supplies of goods or services provided together in the ordinary course of business, where one supply acts as the principal supply and determines the applicable GST rate for the entire bundled transaction.

questions.question_english:
Consider the following transactions:
I. Opening a Basic Savings Bank Deposit Account (BSBDA)
II. Depositing cash exceeding ₹50,000 with a banking company during any one single day
III. Sale or purchase of a motor vehicle other than a two-wheeler
According to Rule 114B of the Income Tax Rules, 1962, quoting of Permanent Account Number (PAN) is mandatory for which of the transactions listed above?
options_english: I and II only
II and III only
I and III only
I, II, and III
questions.explanation_english:
Rule 114B of the Income Tax Rules, 1962 mandates quoting of PAN for specified financial transactions:
1. Opening a bank account: While opening an account with a banking company or cooperative bank generally requires PAN, Rule 114B explicitly carves out an exception for a Basic Savings Bank Deposit Account (BSBDA / Jan Dhan account). Therefore, quoting PAN is NOT mandatory for opening a BSBDA (Statement I is incorrect).
2. Cash deposits: Quoting PAN is mandatory for deposit of cash exceeding ₹50,000 during any one single day with a banking company or cooperative bank (Statement II is correct).
3. Motor vehicles: Quoting PAN is mandatory for the sale or purchase of any motor vehicle or vehicle, other than two-wheeled vehicles (Statement III is correct).
Therefore, quoting PAN is mandatory for transactions II and III only.

आयकर नियम, 1962 का नियम 114B विनिर्दिष्ट वित्तीय लेन-देन के लिए पैन (PAN) उद्धृत करना अनिवार्य बनाता है:
1. बैंक खाता खोलना: सामान्यतः बैंकिंग कंपनी या सहकारी बैंक में खाता खोलने के लिए पैन अनिवार्य है, परंतु नियम 114B स्पष्ट रूप से 'बुनियादी बचत बैंक जमा खाते' (BSBDA / जन-धन खाता) को इससे छूट प्रदान करता है। अतः BSBDA खाता खोलने के लिए पैन अनिवार्य नहीं है (कथन I गलत है)।
2. नकद जमा: किसी बैंकिंग कंपनी या सहकारी बैंक में एक ही दिन के दौरान ₹50,000 से अधिक नकद जमा करने के लिए पैन उद्धृत करना अनिवार्य है (कथन II सही है)।
3. मोटर वाहन: दोपहिया वाहनों को छोड़कर, किसी भी अन्य मोटर वाहन की बिक्री या खरीद के लिए पैन उद्धृत करना अनिवार्य है (कथन III सही है)।
अतः सही उत्तर केवल II और III है।

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Under Rule 114B of the Income Tax Rules 1962, quoting Permanent Account Number is mandatory for specified financial transactions. These include depositing cash exceeding fifty thousand rupees with a banking company in a single day and purchasing or selling motor vehicles other than two-wheeled vehicles. Basic savings accounts do not mandate PAN.

questions.question_english: A government employee receives a Leave Travel Concession (LTC) advance of ₹80,000 but fails to produce travel tickets or undertake the journey within the stipulated period. What administrative and taxation action should the DDO take?
options_english: Permit the employee to refund the balance in the next financial year without interest or tax
Add the entire amount to the employee's salary and grant tax exemption under Section 10(5)
Recover the entire advance amount with penal interest and treat it as taxable salary if not adjusted
Write off the entire amount as administrative expenditure without verifying travel vouchers
questions.explanation_english: Under Central Civil Services (LTC) Rules read with the Income Tax Act, 1961, LTC tax exemption under Section 10(5) and Rule 2B is admissible strictly upon actual travel undertaken and supported by valid proof of expenditure (tickets/boarding passes). If an employee draws an LTC advance but fails to undertake the journey within the prescribed time limit or fails to submit final adjustment bills, the entire advance must be recovered in a single lump sum along with penal interest (typically 2% over GPF interest rate). In taxation terms, any unadjusted advance cannot claim Section 10(5) exemption and forms part of taxable salary for TDS calculation under Section 192.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर C है। सीसीएस (एलटीसी) नियमावली तथा आयकर अधिनियम, 1961 की धारा 10(5) व नियम 2B के अंतर्गत एलटीसी पर कर छूट केवल वास्तविक यात्रा और वैध यात्रा प्रमाणक प्रस्तुत करने पर ही प्राप्त होती है। यदि कोई कर्मचारी अग्रिम लेकर निर्धारित अवधि में यात्रा नहीं करता या समायोजन बिल प्रस्तुत नहीं करता, तो आहरण एवं संवितरण अधिकारी (DDO) द्वारा अग्रिम की संपूर्ण राशि दंडात्मक ब्याज सहित एकमुश्त वसूल की जाती है। कर की दृष्टि से, असमायोजित अग्रिम पर धारा 10(5) की छूट नहीं मिलती और इसे टीडीएस गणना हेतु वेतन में जोड़कर कर योग्य माना जाता है।

key_facts: Printed answer key: (C) Recover the advance in lump sum with penal interest, and treat the unadjusted amount as taxable salary

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Under LTC rules and Income Tax provisions, LTC advances must be backed by actual travel and proof within the stipulated time. If an employee fails to utilize the advance, it must be refunded in full immediately along with penal interest. Furthermore, no tax exemption under Section 10(5) can be claimed, and any default is treated as taxable salary.

questions.question_english: Which of the following legal consequences applies if a Drawing and Disbursing Officer (DDO) fails to deduct TDS, or deducts TDS but fails to deposit it into the Central Government account within the prescribed time limit?
options_english: The DDO's personal Permanent Account Number (PAN) is permanently cancelled.
The DDO is liable for mandatory interest, monetary penalty, and prosecution under Section 276B.
The school's financial recognition is permanently withdrawn by the Directorate of Education.
The tax liability is entirely waived off for both the employer and employee.
questions.explanation_english:
Under the Income Tax Act, 1961, failure by a Drawing and Disbursing Officer (DDO) to deduct or deposit TDS attracts severe statutory liabilities:
1. Interest under Section 201(1A): Mandatory interest is levied at 1% per month (or part of a month) for delay in deducting tax, and at 1.5% per month (or part of a month) for delay in depositing deducted tax into the government account.
2. Penalty under Section 271C: A penalty equal to the amount of tax failed to be deducted may be imposed.
3. Prosecution under Section 276B: If a person fails to pay to the credit of the Central Government the tax deducted at source, they shall be punishable with rigorous imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than three months but which may extend to seven years, along with a fine.

Personal PAN cancellation or withdrawal of school recognition are not statutory penalties under the Income Tax Act.
questions.explanation_hindi:
आयकर अधिनियम, 1961 के तहत, आहरण एवं संवितरण अधिकारी (DDO) द्वारा टीडीएस (TDS) की कटौती न करने या उसे सरकारी खाते में जमा न करने पर गंभीर वैधानिक परिणाम लागू होते हैं:
1. धारा 201(1A) के तहत ब्याज: कर कटौती में देरी के लिए 1% प्रति माह (या माह का भाग) और काटे गए कर को सरकारी खाते में जमा करने में देरी के लिए 1.5% प्रति माह (या माह का भाग) की दर से अनिवार्य ब्याज देय होता है।
2. धारा 271C के तहत शास्ति: न काटे गए कर की राशि के बराबर जुर्माना लगाया जा सकता है।
3. धारा 276B के तहत अभियोजन: यदि कोई व्यक्ति स्रोत पर काटे गए कर को केंद्र सरकार के खाते में जमा करने में विफल रहता है, तो वह कठोर कारावास (न्यूनतम 3 माह से लेकर अधिकतम 7 वर्ष तक) और जुर्माने से दंडनीय होगा।

व्यक्तिगत पैन को रद्द करना या स्कूल की मान्यता रद्द करना आयकर अधिनियम के तहत निर्धारित दंड नहीं हैं।
questions.topic: Income Tax and GST Basics for School Administration
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) The DDO is liable for interest, penalty, and prosecution under Section 276B.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: prosecution under Section 276B. Failure by a Drawing and Disbursing Officer to deduct tax at source or to deposit deducted tax into the government treasury attracts mandatory interest penalties under Section 201(1A). Additionally, persistent failure without reasonable cause can result in financial penalties and criminal prosecution under Section 276B of the Income Tax Act 1961.

questions.question_english: A senior Post Graduate Teacher (PGT) informs the DDO in the month of April that they wish to be taxed under the Old Tax Regime for monthly salary TDS purposes. At the time of filing their annual Income Tax Return in July, can the teacher legally modify their choice and switch to the New Tax Regime?
questions.question_hindi: एक वरिष्ठ स्नातकोत्तर शिक्षक (PGT) अप्रैल माह में DDO को सूचित करते हैं कि वे मासिक वेतन TDS के प्रयोजन हेतु पुरानी कर व्यवस्था के तहत कर कटौती कराना चाहते हैं। जुलाई में अपना वार्षिक आयकर रिटर्न (ITR) दाखिल करते समय, क्या शिक्षक कानूनी रूप से अपना विकल्प बदलकर नई कर व्यवस्था में जा सकते हैं?
options_english: Yes, individuals having only salary income are fully entitled to switch tax regimes at the time of filing their ITR under Section 139(1).
No, an employee who has declared their option to the DDO is legally bound by it and cannot alter it during ITR filing.
Yes, but only after obtaining formal written approval from the jurisdictional Income Tax Assessing Officer.
No, the choice between the Old and New Tax Regimes is a once-in-a-lifetime irrevocable election for all taxpayers.
options_hindi: हाँ, केवल वेतन आय वाले व्यक्ति धारा 139(1) के तहत अपना ITR दाखिल करते समय कर व्यवस्था बदलने के पूर्ण हकदार हैं।
नहीं, जिस कर्मचारी ने DDO को अपने विकल्प की घोषणा कर दी है, वह उससे बाध्य है और ITR फाइलिंग के समय इसे बदल नहीं सकता।
हाँ, लेकिन केवल क्षेत्राधिकार वाले आयकर निर्धारण अधिकारी (AO) से औपचारिक लिखित अनुमति प्राप्त करने के बाद।
नहीं, पुरानी और नई कर व्यवस्था के बीच चयन सभी करदाताओं के लिए जीवनकाल में केवल एक बार किया जाने वाला अपरिवर्तनीय विकल्प है।
questions.explanation_english:
According to CBDT Circular No. 04/2023 (clarifying TDS under Section 192 read with Section 115BAC), the intimation made by an employee to their employer/DDO regarding their intended tax regime at the beginning of the financial year is purely for the purpose of monthly tax deduction at source (TDS). This initial intimation to the DDO does not amount to exercising the statutory option before the Income Tax Department.
An individual who derives income only from salary (and does not have business or professional income under Section 44AB) has the complete statutory freedom to switch between the Old Tax Regime and the New Tax Regime at the time of filing their annual return of income under Section 139(1). If excess tax was deducted by the DDO due to the April intimation, the employee can claim a tax refund while filing the return under their newly chosen regime.
questions.explanation_hindi:
सीबीडीटी (CBDT) के परिपत्र सं. 04/2023 (धारा 115BAC के तहत वेतन पर TDS स्पष्टीकरण) के अनुसार, वित्तीय वर्ष के प्रारंभ में कर्मचारी द्वारा अपने नियोक्ता/DDO को दी गई कर व्यवस्था की सूचना केवल मासिक वेतन से स्रोत पर कर कटौती (TDS) की गणना के लिए होती है। DDO को दी गई यह सूचना आयकर विभाग के समक्ष अंतिम वैधानिक विकल्प नहीं मानी जाती।
एक वेतनभोगी व्यक्ति (जिसके पास व्यापार या पेशे से आय नहीं है) धारा 139(1) के तहत अपना वार्षिक आयकर रिटर्न दाखिल करते समय पुरानी और नई कर व्यवस्था के बीच बदलाव करने के लिए पूरी तरह स्वतंत्र होता है। यदि DDO द्वारा पुरानी व्यवस्था के अनुसार अधिक कर काट लिया गया था और रिटर्न में नई व्यवस्था फायदेमंद रहती है, तो कर्मचारी रिटर्न दाखिल करते समय नई व्यवस्था चुनकर अतिरिक्त कर का रिफंड प्राप्त कर सकता है।

Central Information Commissioner (2012) categorically held that details of an employee's salary deductions, income tax returns, TDS statements, and personal assets qualify as personal information protected under Section 8(1)(j). questions.explanation_english: Under Section 194C of the Income Tax Act, 1961, any specified person (including a school DDO/principal) responsible for paying any sum to a resident contractor for carrying out any work (including transport, maintenance, catering, housekeeping, security, etc.) must deduct tax at source. Once the aggregate crosses ₹1,00,000, TDS is applicable on the entire cumulative amount at 1% for individual/HUF contractors and 2% for corporate/firm contractors.

questions.question_english: What is the statutory rate of interest charged under Section 201(1A) of the Income Tax Act, 1961 for delayed deposit of TDS (i.e., where tax has been deducted but not paid to the government account)?

questions.explanation_english:
Under Section 201(1A) of the Income Tax Act, 1961, if a deductor fails to deduct or pay TDS, mandatory simple interest is levied as follows:

1. For failure/delay in deducting tax: Simple interest at 1.0% per month or part of a month, from the date on which tax was deductible to the date on which tax is actually deducted.
2. For failure/delay in depositing tax after deduction: Simple interest at 1.5% per month or part of a month, from the date on which tax was deducted to the date on which such tax is actually paid/deposited into the government treasury.

Since this question specifically asks about delayed deposit (tax deducted but not deposited), the applicable rate is 1.5% per month or part of a month. This interest cannot be waived and must be paid before filing the quarterly return.

questions.question_english: A teacher informs the DDO that they have an additional income of ₹50,000 from Bank Fixed Deposits and requests that tax on it be deducted at source from their salary. What should the DDO do under the Income Tax Act?
options_english: Reject the request as bank interest TDS must be deducted exclusively by the concerned commercial bank
Direct the employee to obtain a formal No Objection Certificate (NOC) from the Income Tax Department
Advise the employee to deposit Advance Tax independently instead of adjusting through salary TDS
Include this ₹50,000 under 'Income from Other Sources' in the tax computation and deduct TDS accordingly
questions.explanation_english: Under Section 192(2B) of the Income Tax Act, 1961, a salaried employee is statutorily entitled to declare to the DDO any income chargeable under any other head of income (such as 'Income from Other Sources', including bank interest or dividend income). Upon receiving such a written declaration from the employee, the DDO is legally required to take this additional income into account while computing total taxable income and deduct the appropriate higher TDS from the monthly salary. However, the DDO cannot take into account any loss under other heads except under the head 'Income from House Property'.
